title: Lord, Thou Hast Heard Thy Servant Cry
description: Lord, Thou Hast Heard Thy Servant Cry in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 118, part 2, headed “Public praise for deliverance from death”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, thou hast heard thy ser-vant cry, And res-cu'd from the grave; Now shall he live: (and none can die If God re-solve to save.)

lines: Lord, thou hast heard thy servant cry,
Now shall he live: (and none can die
Thy praise, more constant than before,
Thy hand that hath chastis'd him sore,
Open the gates of Zion now,
The house where all the righteous go
Among th' assemblies of thy saints
There we have told thee our complaints,
And there we speak thy praise.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
